text: Eighty-eight year old female from Sunrise Assisted Living, aide says she fell getting out of bed at 0200 and couldn't get up. Right leg is shortened and externally rotated. She's on Coumadin. Pain 7 out of 10, gave 25 mics of fentanyl IN.
facts: right leg shortened and externally rotated
notes: cat=trauma. Aide = facility staff = family (source 'aide'). The facility name is an origin, not a destination. Time of the fall = symptom.onset.

text: onset was at fourteen twelve witnessed by her daughter at the kitchen table
notes: cat=stroke. Dispatch rule. Clock time of a witnessed onset = symptom.onset, not LKW (4). The time clause is the medic's; the witnessing is sourced to the daughter who saw it.

text: Bystander CPR in progress when we arrived, and they had shocked him once with the gym's AED. We took over compressions at 0715, he's in PEA. Intubated with a 7.5, 23 at the lip, good waveform, end tidal 14. Epi 1 milligram IV at 0718 and 0722.
notes: cat=arrest. Bystander CPR and our CPR are separate events. One phrase with two times = two epinephrine events sharing dose and route.

text: Sixty year old male, nausea and vomiting since 0400, took two Pepto at home. Home meds are metformin, Jardiance and Lipitor. We gave Zofran 4 milligrams IV at 0630. Sugar 214.
notes: cat=general. Pepto = bismuth subsalicylate (own dose = meds.list), Jardiance = empagliflozin, Lipitor = atorvastatin. SGLT2 is not an anticoagulant.

text: i saw the whole thing the car was going maybe forty and hit him right in the crosswalk he flew like ten feet and didnt move for a minute i put pressure on his leg it was bleeding a lot
speaker: witness
facts: hit by a car in the crosswalk, thrown 10 feet
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=trauma. 'Maybe forty' is hedged: not in the mechanism. 'Like ten feet' approximator dropped. A bystander's 'bleeding a lot' is not an injury found.

text: stab wound to the right groin bright red bleeding we packed the wound with combat gauze and are holding pressure bleeding controlled patient states hes allergic to penicillin pressure ninety two over sixty heart rate one twenty eight
facts: stab wound to the right groin
notes: cat=trauma. Only the allergy is the patient's.

text: ok uh second round of amio one fifty at oh four twenty two um compressions continuing rhythm check coming up and uh last end tidal was twenty eight
notes: cat=arrest. 'Rhythm check coming up' is a plan: nothing. Ongoing compressions = cpr by crew.

text: forty five year old male stung by a bee on the golf course about fifteen minutes ago his playing partner hit him with an epipen before we got there throat feels tight diffuse hives wheezes on the right we gave a second epi point three IM at eleven twenty two and solumedrol one twenty five iv allergic to bee stings and codeine
notes: cat=medical. EpiPen given before arrival by someone else (playing partner) = meds.given by bystander, no dose/route said. Solu-Medrol = methylprednisolone.

text: thirty eight year old male iv drug user abscess on the left forearm at an injection site looks infected temp thirty nine point one heart rate one twenty two pressure one oh four over sixty two he says he last used heroin this morning
notes: cat=sepsis. Heroin is an illicit drug, not a medication: no meds.list, no meds.given.

text: Sixty-one year old female, syncopal episode in church, witnessed by her husband, down for maybe 30 seconds. Alert and oriented times four now, denies chest pain. Orthostatics: lying 128 over 76 heart rate 72, standing 104 over 68 heart rate 102. 12-lead shows sinus rhythm, no ectopy.
notes: cat=medical. Syncope is not stroke-like: 'witnessed' gives no stroke.onset_witnessed. 'Maybe 30 seconds' hedged. Lying and standing = two readings each. A 12-lead that 'shows' a rhythm gives no time and no 'attached', so no ecg fact.

text: Sixty-nine year old male, cough with green sputum that started 4 days ago, now short of breath. Rhonchi in the right lower lobe, temp 39.4, sats 88 on room air, resps 28, heart rate 118. Probably pneumonia. Put him on 4 liters nasal cannula, sats up to 93.
notes: cat=sepsis. 'Probably pneumonia' = respiratory (4e example wording).

text: Regional, Medic 21, trauma alert, ten minutes out. Eighty-one year old male, driver in a head-on collision at about 40 miles an hour, on Pradaxa. Flail segment on the left chest wall, sats 88 on a non-rebreather. Pressure 90 over 56. GCS 15. We're going to hold off on TXA until we talk to you.
facts: driver in a head-on collision at 40 miles an hour
flail segment on the left chest wall
notes: cat=trauma. Pradaxa = dabigatran. Held TXA is a plan/denial: no meds.given.

text: Sugar was 32 on arrival, patient is diaphoretic and only responding to pain. Established a 20 gauge in the right hand, gave D10, 150 mLs, recheck at 5 minutes was 88, then 131. She's now alert and oriented. Takes Lantus and metformin.
notes: cat=medical. Three glucose readings = three facts. D10 = dextrose; no route said. Lantus = insulin glargine. 'She's' is a pronoun: no sex.

text: we called it at oh five twelve after thirty minutes of cpr asystole throughout end tidal never got above ten medical control agreed family is with him
notes: cat=arrest. 'Never got above ten' is a bound, not a reading: no etco2 (5b ranges). Time of death has no key.

text: found down in the bedroom unwitnessed cold to touch asystole on arrival daughter just showed us a polst it says dnr so we are not starting compressions
notes: cat=arrest. No CPR (explicitly not started). The POLST was read by the crew = medic role. 'Unwitnessed' gives no stroke key (not stroke-like).

text: Sixty-six year old male, witnessed arrest at the dinner table, wife started CPR. We found him in V-fib, shocked at 200 joules at 1906, IO in the right humerus, 1 of epi IO at 1909, second shock at 1910, amiodarone 300 at 1912. i-gel size 4 in, end tidal 18.
notes: cat=arrest. An arrest is not stroke-like: 'witnessed' gives no stroke.onset_witnessed. Each shock is its own event. Wife's CPR: by 'family'. Rhythm has no key.

text: Update for Kaiser, we got ROSC at 0431 after two shocks. End tidal jumped from 22 to 41. Pressure 88 over 50, heart rate 114. Still unresponsive, King airway in place, sats 94. Post-ROSC 12-lead done at 0436 and attached. ETA 9.
notes: cat=arrest. ROSC itself has no key. A summary count of shocks = one fact with count in detail (guide example '2 shocks').

text: Thirty-one year old female, 34 weeks pregnant, slipped on ice and fell onto her back. No vaginal bleeding, she says the baby's moving. Lower back pain 4 out of 10. Pressure 122 over 78, heart rate 96. Taking her to Labor and Delivery at Good Samaritan, 14 minutes.
facts: slipped on ice and fell onto her back
notes: cat=trauma. Fetal movement and bleeding denial have no key. '14 minutes' after the destination = ETA.

text: six year old boy fell off the monkey bars onto his outstretched arm um obvious deformity to the right forearm distal pulses intact cap refill under two pain eight out of ten we splinted it and gave him thirty micrograms of fentanyl intranasal moms on the way
facts: fell off the monkey bars onto his outstretched arm
obvious deformity to the right forearm
notes: cat=trauma. 'Cap refill under two' has no key.

text: Fifty year old female, sharp chest pain worse with a deep breath, just got back from a long flight. Heart rate 118, sats 91 on room air, resps 24. Pt denies blood thinners, takes birth control. NKDA. 12-lead done at 1520, sinus tach.
notes: cat=medical. 'Pt denies' = patient role (5b). Birth control is a class, not a named drug: no meds.list. NKDA subjectless = medic.

text: ninety one year old male generalized weakness started three days ago not eating much family says hes a full code takes metoprolol eliquis and tamsulosin nkda blood pressure one oh two over sixty two heart rate fifty two sugar one sixty
notes: cat=general. Generalized weakness is not focal: no stroke keys. 'Takes ...' is a new subjectless clause = medic (4c). List first (metoprolol said first), anticoagulant at 'eliquis'.

text: glucometer just reads high shes been vomiting since yesterday breath smells fruity resps deep at twenty eight shes a type one on an insulin pump husband says the pump site was kinked we gave four of zofran iv
notes: cat=medical. 'Reads high' gives no glucose number (5b). Insulin pump -> insulin (v1_050). The husband's pump-site remark has no key.

text: Twenty-four year old male, wife says he had a seizure about ten minutes ago and another one started as we walked in. We gave 5 of Versed IM, seizure stopped at 1408. He's postictal, eyes open to voice, GCS 12. Sugar 104. Takes Keppra, wife says he missed his doses this week.
notes: cat=medical. Versed = midazolam, Keppra = levetiracetam. 'Eyes open to voice' gives V; GCS 12 gives only the total. Missed doses are not a stopped drug, and 'Takes Keppra' is subjectless shorthand = medic.

text: Seventy-nine year old male, chest pressure since he woke up at 0500. He's on Xarelto for a-fib and takes atorvastatin. Heart rate 124 irregular, pressure 102 over 60, correction, 108 over 60. 12-lead attached, no STEMI. We held the aspirin, he already took 325 at home.
notes: cat=medical. 'Since he woke up at 0500' is a discovery time: no onset (4c). Correction keeps 108/60 only. Held aspirin = no meds.given; the home 325 = meds.list (one merged list fact at its first mention).

text: Update on her: speech was garbled on scene but it's clear now. Face is symmetric. Left arm still drifts. Pressure 172 over 90, correction, 176 over 90.
notes: cat=stroke. Resolved garbled speech: current state wins (speech 0) and it is not a deficit. 'Speech clear' = no RACE value.

text: Lift assist, eighty-three year old female slid out of her wheelchair onto the carpet, no injuries, denies hitting her head, denies pain. Walker next to the bed, oxygen concentrator running in the corner.
facts: slid out of her wheelchair onto the carpet
oxygen concentrator running in the corner
notes: cat=general. Fall without injury: mechanism yes, injuries none. A concentrator in the room is a scene note, not on_oxygen.

text: Mercy General, Medic 14. We're coming to you with a 58-year-old male, crushing substernal chest pain that started about 40 minutes ago. 12-lead done at 0942 shows ST elevation in two, three and aVF, it's attached. We gave 324 of aspirin PO and point four nitro sublingual. Pressure 142 over 88, heart rate 96, sats 97 on room air. ETA 11 minutes.
notes: cat=medical. Hailing 'Mercy General' + 'coming to you' = destination. 'About' dropped from onset. Doses carry no unit because none was said ('324 of aspirin', 'point four nitro'). The ST-elevation reading has no key; the 12-lead gives time and attached.

text: Um, she, she went to bed around eleven last night, she was fine, and I found her like this at six this morning. She's not on any blood thinners. My son says she fell last week too.
speaker: husband
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=stroke. Dispatch rule: no symptom words. 'Last night' adds pm; 'around' dropped. Found at six = discovery, no time. The son's relayed past fall has no key.

text: Forty-one year old female, grease fire in the kitchen, partial thickness burns to both forearms and the right hand. Pain 9 out of 10. 50 mics of fentanyl IV at 1841. No airway involvement, no singed nasal hairs.
facts: partial thickness burns to both forearms and the right hand
notes: cat=trauma. Denied airway findings give nothing.

text: Good Sam, Medic 9, inbound stroke alert, 74-year-old female, LKW 1615 per husband, onset witnessed. Right-sided hemiparesis, she's aphasic, eyes deviated left. RACE of 7. Husband says no blood thinners. Pressure 210 over 110, sugar 128, 12-lead attached. ETA 7.
notes: cat=stroke. 'Per husband' governs only the LKW; 'onset witnessed' is a subjectless shorthand clause = medic. Hemiparesis has no severity: no RACE arm/leg. RACE total gives nothing.

text: Fire had already given 4 of Narcan intranasal before we arrived, minimal response. We gave another 0.4 milligrams IV at 2231 and he's breathing better, resps went from 4 to 14. Pinpoint pupils, end tidal came down from 68 to 41. Needle and a spoon on the table next to him.
facts: needle and a spoon on the table next to him
notes: cat=medical. Two naloxone events (fire, then crew). 'From 4 to 14' and 'from 68 to 41' are two readings each. Pupils have no key.

text: Assault, struck in the head with a bat per police. Four centimeter laceration to the right parietal scalp. GCS is 13, eyes 3, verbal 4, motor 6. Pressure 162 over 94, heart rate 64, uh, correction, heart rate 54.
facts: struck in the head with a bat
4 centimeter laceration to the right parietal scalp
notes: cat=trauma. Police are not family: bystander role with source 'police'. 'Assault' is the medic's opening word = medic complaint.

text: He just grabbed his chest and fell over at the table, I started pushing on his chest like the lady on the phone told me, maybe five minutes. He takes Plavix and Lipitor. He's a full code, do everything.
speaker: wife
facts: grabbed his chest and fell over
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=arrest. Compressions by the wife = cpr by family; 'maybe five minutes' hedged, no detail. Plavix is an antiplatelet: no anticoagulant.

text: Eighty-two year old female, CHF history, woke up short of breath, crackles to the mid fields, sats 82 room air. Put her on CPAP at 7.5 of PEEP, gave 0.4 nitro SL at 0310 and another 0.4 SL at 0315. Now satting 93, resps down from 36 to 24, pressure 188 over 102, EtCO2 34.
notes: cat=medical. Two nitro doses = two facts. CPAP = procedure + on_oxygen true. 'From 36 to 24' = two readings.

text: He went up for a header and clashed heads with another kid, he was out for maybe ten seconds. He's got a bad cut over his left eye. He's fifteen. His mom told me he's allergic to amoxicillin.
speaker: coach
facts: went up for a header and clashed heads with another kid
bad cut over his left eye
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=trauma. Coach = bystander. Nested relay: the allergy is the mother's (family, source 'mom'). LOC duration hedged and has no key.

text: it started around two this afternoon right here in my lower right side its like an eight i threw up twice im not pregnant my last period was two weeks ago i dont take any medicines and im not allergic to anything
speaker: patient
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=general. 'This afternoon' adds pm. Pregnancy denial and 'no medicines' give no key.

text: Twelve year old boy on a bike hit a curb and went over the handlebars, no helmet, witnessed by his friend. Hematoma above the right eye. GCS 14 on our arrival, now 12, E3 V4 M5.
facts: bike hit a curb, went over the handlebars, no helmet
notes: cat=trauma. Witnessed trauma mechanism: no stroke.onset_witnessed (4c). Two GCS totals = two readings; components belong to the 12.

text: Husband says she was last normal at 10 pm last night, he found her confused this morning. Sugar 29. Gave 25 grams of D50 IV, recheck 112, she's alert and knows where she is now.
notes: cat=medical. Hypoglycemia on a non-stroke dispatch: 'last normal at 10 pm' gives no stroke.lkw (4c). 'Found her confused this morning' = discovery, no time; confusion sourced to the husband who found her.

text: low speed rear end collision restrained driver no airbag deployment sixty two year old female complaining of neck stiffness pain three out of ten no midline tenderness denies blood thinners takes lisinopril gcs fifteen a and o times four
facts: low speed rear-end collision, restrained driver, no airbag deployment
notes: cat=trauma. Subjectless 'denies blood thinners' = medic, anticoagulant 'none'. A&O x4 = A.

text: uh she's on, um, eliquis for a-fib, last known well was one forty, uh, per the caregiver, and she can't look to the right past midline
notes: cat=stroke. 'One forty' -> 1:40. 'Can't look to the right' = G.F.A.S.T. gaze 1 + deficit, no RACE gaze (5b).

text: Nine year old girl, pedestrian struck by a car at about 25 miles an hour, thrown onto the hood. Mom says she didn't lose consciousness. Abrasions to the left hip and a deformity of the left lower leg, pain 9 out of 10. Splinted the leg, gave fentanyl 1 mic per kilo intranasal, that's 30 mics.
facts: pedestrian struck by a car at 25 miles an hour, thrown onto the hood
deformity of the left lower leg
notes: cat=trauma. Weight-based order resolves to the dose actually given (30 mcg). Mom's LOC denial has no key.

text: Thirty-five year old male, police asked us to evaluate, he's pacing and yelling, says people are following him. His mother says he stopped taking his Abilify a month ago. He's alert, heart rate 124, sugar 98. Haldol 5 IM and Ativan 2 IM, both at 1305.
notes: cat=general. Stopped drug (Abilify) = no meds.list (5b). Haldol = haloperidol, Ativan = lorazepam; 'both at 1305' applies the time to each.

text: thirty year old male found in a gas station bathroom pulseless and apneic security guard says he went in there about twenty minutes ago needle on the floor next to him were doing cpr gave two milligrams of narcan iv igel placed end tidal sixty on the first breaths
facts: needle on the floor next to him
notes: cat=arrest. The security guard's time is when he entered, not a symptom onset: no fact. 'were' = we're (ASR).

text: neighbor found him on the kitchen floor this morning nobody saw it happen she last talked to him at twenty two hundred last night and he was normal
notes: cat=stroke. Dispatch rule: no symptom words, still labeled. Found = false, sourced to the neighbor who found him (5b). 24-hour time stays '2200' (no pm).

text: Sixty-eight year old male, right facial droop, his right arm drifts down, right leg he can't lift off the bed at all, and he can't get any words out, just nods. Eyes are midline. Last known well 0845 per his wife. Sugar 142, pressure 188 over 96.
notes: cat=stroke. Unqualified droop = facial 2. Can't lift leg = leg 2. Can't get words out = severe aphasia 2. 'Eyes midline' = gaze 0 on both scales. Only the LKW is the wife's.

text: Son thinks she might take something for her heart, maybe a water pill, but he's not sure. He thinks she's around eighty, and she might have fallen, he doesn't know when.
notes: cat=general. All hedged; drug class only.

text: Patient says she broke out in hives this morning after her first dose of a new antibiotic. No trouble breathing, no lip swelling. She's allergic to penicillin and latex, takes lisinopril and Synthroid. We gave diphenhydramine 25 milligrams by mouth.
notes: cat=general. 'A new antibiotic' is a class: no meds.list, no allergy. Synthroid = levothyroxine. Home meds vs given med kept apart.

text: forty two year old female right lower quadrant abdominal pain since last night around twenty three hundred nauseated vomited three times pain eight out of ten worse with movement gave zofran four iv going to give fentanyl once the second line is in pressure one twenty eight over eighty four heart rate one oh two temp thirty seven point nine
notes: cat=general. Planned fentanyl gives nothing. 24-hour time stays '2300' (no pm added); 'around' dropped.

text: restrained passenger t boned on her side airbags deployed shes twenty six weeks pregnant complaining of abdominal pain seven out of ten seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen fetal heart tones one forty on the doppler pressure one ten over sixty eight
facts: restrained passenger, t-boned on her side, airbags deployed
seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen
notes: cat=trauma. Fetal heart tones 140 are NOT vitals.hr. 'Pregnant'/'her' are not sex descriptors: no patient.sex.

text: Thirty year old female, patient states her boyfriend punched her in the face and kicked her in the stomach. She's 20 weeks pregnant. Swelling and bruising around the left eye, abrasion to the left cheek. Abdominal pain 5 out of 10, no vaginal bleeding.
facts: punched in the face and kicked in the stomach
punched in the face and kicked in the stomach
swelling and bruising around the left eye
notes: cat=trauma. Only the mechanism clause is the patient's; the weeks and findings are the medic's.

text: Hi, I'm her aide at the group home. She's had a temp of 101 since last night and her urine smells really strong, looks like another UTI to me. Normally she's chatty but today she's confused, doesn't know where she is. She takes Depakote and Keppra, and she's allergic to sulfa.
speaker: aide
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=sepsis. Group-home aide = family, source 'aide'. 101 F -> 38.3. Caregiver-stated source = urinary. Depakote = divalproex.

text: Seventy-eight year old female, husband found her unresponsive in the recliner around 1530, last seen normal at 1500. He says she's full code. She's on Eliquis and metoprolol. Fire started CPR at 1538, we've shocked twice, now asystole.
notes: cat=arrest. Non-stroke call: 'last seen normal at 1500' gives no stroke.lkw; 'found at 1530' is a discovery time. 'She's on Eliquis' is a new sentence = medic.

text: Twenty-nine year old female, fever of 101.2 since this afternoon with body aches, took ibuprofen at 1500. Heart rate 104, pressure 116 over 72, sats 98 on room air. Alert and oriented, no other complaints.
notes: cat=sepsis. CONTRAST: fever alone, no source stated -> no infection.suspected. Own ibuprofen dose = meds.list. 101.2 F -> 38.4.

text: Thirty-four year old female, palpitations since about 1600, heart rate 212, narrow complex. We tried a vagal maneuver, no change. Adenosine 6 milligrams rapid IV push at 1648, converted briefly then back into SVT, second dose 12 milligrams IV at 1651. Pressure holding at 118 over 74.
notes: cat=medical. Repeat dose = second fact. A failed attempt keeps its result in detail ('no change'). 'About' dropped; symptom.onset keeps 'since'.

text: yeah im diabetic i took my insulin this morning but skipped breakfast um my sugar was like forty when i checked it at ten my wife gave me some orange juice
speaker: patient
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=medical. Orange juice is not a drug. The check time has no key.

text: i took two of my nitro pills before they got here and a baby aspirin the pains like a six now it was a nine im allergic to morphine
speaker: patient
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=medical. Patient's own pre-arrival doses = meds.list. 'Like a six' approximator dropped; now and earlier = two readings.

text: Eighty-four year old female from Oak Grove nursing home, nurse says she's been more confused than usual since yesterday. Temp 101.8, heart rate 112, pressure 88 over 52, resps 24, end tidal 26. Foley's draining cloudy dark urine, looks like urosepsis.
notes: cat=sepsis. Nursing-home nurse = family. Confusion goes to consciousness C, not complaint (v1_039). 101.8 F -> 38.8.

text: 72-year-old female, history of COPD, severe shortness of breath since this morning. Resps 32, sats 84 on room air, end tidal 52. We gave albuterol 5 milligrams with Atrovent point five by neb, then put her on CPAP at 8. Sats now 91.
notes: cat=medical. Atrovent = ipratropium; 'by neb' covers both drugs of the combined treatment. CPAP is a procedure and oxygen delivery (on_oxygen true); 8 is pressure. COPD history has no key.

text: Two year old girl, febrile seizure per dad, lasted about a minute, she's crying and consolable now. Temp 103.1 rectal. No allergies.
notes: cat=medical. 103.1 F -> 39.5 C. Seizure duration has no key. 'Girl' is a sex descriptor.

text: GFAST is four out of four. Last known well was 10:30 this morning per the neighbor who had coffee with her. Taking her to Regional Medical as a stroke alert, ETA 16.
notes: cat=stroke. 4 of 4 = all items 1 (4d). 'This morning' adds am. Neighbor = bystander.

text: Dispatched as a fall, but she's got a new right facial droop and slurred speech. Daughter says she was fine at noon when they had lunch. Her right arm is weak, she can't lift it off the bed.
notes: cat=general. Non-stroke dispatch, but the words describe stroke-like symptoms, so stroke keys apply (4c). 'Dispatched as a fall' is not a complaint. Can't lift arm = RACE arm 2.

text: eighty nine year old female from maple ridge aide says shes had a draining wound on her sacrum and now she only opens her eyes to voice the wound looks infected foul smell pressure eighty four over forty six heart rate one twenty two temp thirty five point eight end tidal twenty two eighteen gauge right ac and a twenty in the left hand dnr on file per the aide
notes: cat=sepsis. The aide's clause covers the wound and the eyes-to-voice state; 'looks infected' is the medic's. Two lines at different sites = two facts. Hypothermic 35.8 stays as said.

text: St. Luke's, Medic 3, en route with a 55-year-old male post-arrest. Collapsed at the gym, bystanders did CPR and gave one AED shock, ROSC before our arrival. Now GCS 7, E1 V2 M4, pressure 104 over 70, heart rate 58, sats 98 on 15 liters, end tidal 36. 12-lead done at 1802 shows an anterior STEMI. ETA 6 minutes.
notes: cat=arrest. Total and components both said, each labeled. GCS gives no ACVPU letter.

text: Three year old boy, mom says his fever was 104 at home. Temp now 102.2 tympanic, heart rate 160, he's alert and drinking fine. No meds, no allergies.
notes: cat=sepsis. CONTRAST: fever only, no infection.suspected. Home and current temps are two readings. 'No meds' gives no key.

text: Eighty year old male, daughter says his doctor diagnosed pneumonia yesterday and started him on amoxicillin. Today he's more short of breath and confused. Sats 86 on room air, resps 32, temp 38.3, pressure 96 over 60.
notes: cat=sepsis. Caregiver-stated source = respiratory (family). The new sentence 'Today he's...' is the medic's.

text: Seventy-one year old female, husband says she tested positive for COVID on Monday. Now short of breath, sats 84 on room air and 90 on 6 liters. Temp 38.9, resps 30, heart rate 116. She's confused. End tidal 29.
notes: cat=sepsis. COVID stated by the husband = respiratory source (family). Room air then 6 L = two sats and both on_oxygen values.

text: Husband says she was fine at 1930 when he went to take a shower.
notes: cat=stroke. Dispatch rule (4c): stroke dispatch -> LKW labeled with no symptom words.

text: Epi one milligram IV at 2214. Amiodarone 300, correction, 150 at 2215, the first 300 went in at 2208. Fourth shock at 2216, 360 joules.
notes: cat=arrest. The 2215 dose is corrected to 150; the earlier 300 at 2208 is a separate event, not the corrected value.

text: um so shes forty seven fever and a cough since tuesday temp here is thirty eight point six sats ninety five heart rate ninety eight uh she says shes had her flu shot takes nothing daily no allergies
notes: cat=sepsis. CONTRAST: fever and cough, but no suspected source is stated -> no infection.suspected. No sex ('shes'). Fever goes in temp, cough is the complaint.

text: Unrestrained driver, rollover MVC with ejection. Twenty-eight year old male, GCS 9, E2 V2 M5. Open fracture of the right femur, we put a tourniquet on at 2340, and the pelvis is unstable. Pressure 86 over 50, heart rate 132. Full spinal motion restriction. TXA 1 gram IV at 2348.
facts: unrestrained driver, rollover mvc with ejection
open fracture of the right femur
notes: cat=trauma. Mechanism also gives complaint.chief (4e). Injuries as one list fact. TXA = tranexamic acid.

text: Eight year old boy, asthma attack, mom says he used his albuterol inhaler four times before we got here with no relief. Tripoding, sats 90 on room air, resps 40, heart rate 148. We gave albuterol 2.5 by neb on 8 liters of oxygen, sats now 96. Mom says he's allergic to amoxicillin.
notes: cat=medical. Patient's own inhaler doses before arrival = meds.list (mom's statement); crew neb = meds.given. 'Boy' is a sex descriptor. Room air then oxygen = on_oxygen false and true.

text: seventeen year old male high school football helmet to helmet collision coach says he never lost consciousness complains of neck pain numbness and tingling in both hands and he cant move his legs full spinal motion restriction in place
facts: high school football, helmet to helmet collision
notes: cat=trauma. Suspected spinal injury: numbness and 'can't move his legs' give no stroke.deficits and no G.F.A.S.T. (4c, 4d). The coach's LOC denial has no key.

text: Sixty-three year old female, patient states she's had burning with urination since Sunday and now chills. Temp 38.7, heart rate 106, pressure 132 over 80. Alert and oriented. Allergic to sulfa and codeine.
notes: cat=sepsis. CONTRAST: the patient describes a urinary symptom but no one states a suspected infection -> no infection.suspected (4e needs the crew or a caregiver to state a source).

text: Twenty-six year old female, 9 weeks pregnant per patient, vaginal bleeding and cramping since this morning, soaking about a pad an hour. Pressure 104 over 66, heart rate 112. Allergic to ibuprofen.
notes: cat=general. 'Per patient' governs only the weeks.

text: Twenty-two year old female, intentional overdose, roommate says she took a handful of her Seroquel. Empty pill bottle on the bathroom counter. GCS 14. Pressure 96 over 58, heart rate 118, sugar 97.
facts: empty pill bottle on the bathroom counter
notes: cat=medical. Seroquel = quetiapine, her own med mentioned as taken (not given by anyone) = meds.list. A roommate is not family or facility staff = bystander. GCS 14 gives no ACVPU letter.

text: uh found him slumped in the drivers seat unresponsive agonal resps at like six bystander says he was snorting something about twenty minutes ago we bagged him and gave narcan two milligrams intranasal hes now responding to voice sats up to ninety four
notes: cat=medical. The bystander's drug-use report gives no fact (no key for a drug-use time; not a symptom onset). 'like six' approximator dropped. U then V are two readings.

text: GSW to the right chest, single entry wound right anterior chest, no exit found. Absent breath sounds on the right, sats 84. Needle decompression right second intercostal space with a rush of air, sats now 92. Pressure 94 by palp, heart rate 128.
facts: single entry wound right anterior chest

facts.detail: right second intercostal space, rush of air

notes: cat=trauma. BP by palpation gives systolic only. Breath sounds have no key.

text: Four year old boy pulled from the backyard pool by his dad, down time unknown, dad started CPR. We're doing pediatric compressions, bagging with oxygen, IO in the left tibia, epi point one five IO at 1647. End tidal 11.
notes: cat=arrest. 'Down time unknown' gives nothing. Bagging with oxygen = BVM + on_oxygen true.

text: Seventy-four year old male fell about 10 feet off a ladder cleaning gutters and hit his head, he's on Eliquis. Hematoma to the left occiput, GCS 14. Left wrist has an obvious deformity, pain 6 out of 10. We splinted the wrist and put a c-collar on.
facts: fell 10 feet off a ladder, hit his head
notes: cat=trauma. Anticoagulant before list (5b). C-collar recorded as spinal motion restriction with detail.

text: She was completely fine when I talked to her on FaceTime at 8:15, and then I watched her face droop right there on the screen, and her words got all jumbled. She takes Xarelto.
speaker: daughter
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=stroke. Seeing it on a video call = witnessed (5b). Family description = deficits only, no G.F.A.S.T./RACE.

text: post rosc hes bradying down into the thirties we started pacing at eighty milliamps rate of seventy with capture push dose epi ten mics iv at oh three fifty pressure now ninety two over fifty four
notes: cat=arrest. 'Into the thirties' is a range: no hr. Pacer rate 70 is a setting, not vitals.hr. 'mics' = mcg.

text: She's four and she has asthma, I gave her two of her albuterol nebulizer treatments at home, about an hour apart, and she's still wheezing. Her oxygen was 91 on our pulse ox. No allergies.
speaker: mother
notes: cat=other_mic. theme=medical. The child's own prescribed nebs given at home before the call = home doses -> meds.list, not meds.given.

text: Memorial, Medic 5, 12 minutes out with a 71-year-old female, chest pain and shortness of breath since 1400. She's a DNR, POLST is on the fridge. Takes warfarin and furosemide, allergic to morphine. Pressure 96 over 60, heart rate 44, sats 90 on 4 liters, GCS 15. 12-lead done at 1432 and attached, third-degree block. We have not paced her.
facts: chest pain and shortness of breath
notes: cat=general. Radio handoff mixing many keys. 'Have not paced' = no procedure.

text: pd put a tourniquet on the left thigh at twenty one fifty two before we got there gsw to the left thigh bleeding controlled twenty three year old male pressure one hundred over sixty four heart rate one twenty four hes alert txa one gram iv at twenty two oh one two large bore ivs
notes: cat=trauma. PD = police as the 'by' of a pre-arrival procedure; the fact itself is the medic's report. Same-kind lines with a count = one fact with the count in detail.

text: Motorcycle versus car at highway speed, helmeted rider, thirty-five year old male. Closed mid-shaft deformity of the left femur, road rash to the left arm. Pain ten out of ten. Gave ketamine 25 milligrams IV for pain at 1733, traction splint on the left leg. GCS 15.
facts: motorcycle versus car at highway speed, helmeted rider
closed mid-shaft deformity of the left femur
road rash to the left arm
notes: cat=trauma. GCS 15 gives only the total, no ACVPU.

text: gfast two of four face and speech arms and legs are strong eyes are tracking normally sugar is one oh six
notes: cat=stroke. Named positives = 1; named normals = 0 (4d). 'Arms and legs strong' = RACE arm 0 and leg 0. 'Tracking normally' = G.F.A.S.T. gaze 0 only (no deviation statement for RACE). Bare item names give no deficits.

text: seventy six year old male found by his son this morning lethargic and warm to the touch pressure seventy eight over forty heart rate one twenty eight resps thirty end tidal nineteen temp thirty eight point nine only responds to pain septic picture no obvious source
notes: cat=sepsis. 'Found by his son ... lethargic' = source son (5b). 'Warm to the touch' is not a temperature. Septic with no source = unknown.

text: thirty year old male left flank pain radiating to the groin came on suddenly at noon pain ten out of ten hx of kidney stones gave toradol fifteen milligrams iv and fentanyl fifty mics iv at thirteen twenty
notes: cat=general. Toradol = ketorolac. The 13:20 time belongs to the fentanyl only.

text: Construction worker fell approximately 15 feet from scaffolding, landed on his feet then his back. Forty-four year old male. Pelvis unstable on exam, bilateral heel deformities. Pelvic binder applied, SMR maintained. GCS 15. Pressure 98 over 60, heart rate 118, resps 22, sats 96 on room air.
facts: fell 15 feet from scaffolding, landed on his feet then his back
notes: cat=trauma. 'Approximately' dropped. SMR = spinal motion restriction.

text: Stab wound to the left flank, 3 centimeter laceration, bleeding controlled. Patient rates his pain 8 out of 10. We gave fentanyl 50 micrograms IV at 0115. Nineteen year old male, alert and oriented, pressure 118 over 72, heart rate 110.
facts: stab wound to the left flank
notes: cat=trauma. 'Patient rates his pain' = the patient's statement -> patient role.

text: fifty eight year old diabetic male red hot swollen left lower leg started about three days ago that wound on his shin looks infected red streaking up to the knee temp one oh two point four heart rate one oh eight pressure one twenty over seventy sugar three twelve
facts: red hot swollen left lower leg
notes: cat=sepsis. 102.4 F -> 39.1. 'Looks infected' wound = skin.

text: nineteen year old female ate a cookie with peanuts in it known peanut allergy hives all over lips swelling wheezing throughout we gave epi point three milligrams IM in the left thigh at nineteen thirty two benadryl fifty iv and shes on fifteen liters non rebreather pressure ninety over fifty heart rate one thirty
notes: cat=medical. Benadryl = diphenhydramine, within the 'we gave' list = crew. Non-rebreather = on_oxygen true (15 L is flow, no key).

text: So her sugar was 38 when we got there, we gave D10, 250 mLs IV, recheck 142. The right-sided weakness is gone, she's moving all extremities equally and talking normally now.
notes: cat=stroke. Hypoglycemic mimic on a stroke dispatch. Resolved weakness is not a deficit. 'Moves all extremities equally' = G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 0 (listed in 4d); no RACE arm/leg (not a drift/strength statement). 'Talking normally' = both speech 0s (5b).

text: RACE is facial 1, arm 2, leg 1, gaze 1, aphasia 0, total of 5. Last seen normal by her son at 1300.
notes: cat=stroke. Spoken RACE items map to G.F.A.S.T. (4d); aphasia 0 gives no speech label; total gives nothing; bare scores give no deficits (5b).

text: pt is a fifty three yo mail c/o sob that started three days ago worse today sats eighty nine on two leaders nasal canula baseline home oxygen user lung sounds diminished in the bases gave albuterol five neb resps now twenty six
notes: cat=medical. ASR homophones: 'mail' = male, 'leaders' = liters. c/o is medic shorthand (4b).

text: Welfare check, 80-year-old male found on the floor by his landlord, last seen normal yesterday at 1700. No focal deficits, he's moving everything, but he's confused. Temp 34.9, sugar 110. Skin tear on the left elbow.
facts: skin tear on the left elbow
notes: cat=general. Found-down on a non-stroke dispatch without stroke-like signs: no stroke.lkw, no onset_witnessed, no G.F.A.S.T. (4c, 4d). Landlord = bystander.

text: Okay, we're going to get a 12-lead and then give him aspirin if he's not allergic. He denies chest pain, denies shortness of breath. No aspirin given yet. I'll start a line en route.
notes: cat=general. Plans, a conditional and denials: nothing. 'No aspirin given yet' is not meds.given.

text: Wife says he went to bed at ten thirty last night and was normal, he woke up at 6 like this. Now he's got left-sided weakness, slurred speech, and a mild left facial droop. Takes Plavix and atorvastatin, NKDA.
notes: cat=stroke. 'Last night' adds pm. Woke up with it = onset_witnessed false; 'at 6' is a discovery time. Weakness without severity = no RACE arm. Slurred = G.F.A.S.T. speech only (5a). Plavix is an antiplatelet: no anticoagulant.

text: found sitting on the curb outside the bar intoxicated smells of alcohol he admits to about ten beers responds to voice sugar eighty eight small abrasion on the chin security guard says he fell off a bar stool inside declined an iv
notes: cat=general. Security guard = bystander (4c). Declined IV = nothing. Alcohol amount has no key.

text: ok so hes sixty seven chest pain started around nine thirty took two of his own nitro before we got here didnt help much pain is a seven out of ten radiating to the left arm uh we gave three twenty four of aspirin chewed and one more nitro at ten fifteen pressure one thirty eight over eighty
notes: cat=medical. His own nitro before arrival = meds.list (home dose), the crew's nitro = meds.given. 'Chewed' aspirin normalized to route PO. Second nitro has no dose said. No sex descriptor ('hes' is a pronoun).
